q: All are features of an innocent murmur EXCEPT:
o: It does not radiate to the back
It is soft without a thrill
e: Innocent murmurs are systolic (except the venous hum); diastolic murmurs are pathological.

q: Which is NOT a characteristic of a functional (innocent) murmur?
e: Innocent murmurs are short ejection (mid-systolic) murmurs, not pansystolic.

q: Which murmur feature is NOT significant (can be innocent)?
e: A soft musical systolic murmur is Still's murmur, which is innocent.

q: Which statement about heart sounds in children is FALSE?
o: The second sound is closure of the semilunar valves
The first sound is closure of the atrioventricular valves
The second sound normally splits on inspiration
The first heart sound is normally widely split
A third heart sound may be normal
e: The second sound splits physiologically and a third sound can be normal; a fourth sound is abnormal.

q: How is a patent ductus arteriosus closed medically?
e: Prostaglandin E keeps the duct open; inhibitors of prostaglandin synthesis close it.

q: The most common congenital heart lesion in children is:
e: Ventricular septal defect makes up about 30% of congenital heart disease.

q: An oligaemic lung field on chest X-ray is typical of:
e: Right-to-left shunts with pulmonary stenosis reduce the blood flow to the lungs.

q: A plethoric lung field is seen in:
e: Left-to-right shunts increase the pulmonary blood flow.

q: A newborn with Down syndrome should be screened for which heart lesion?
e: Atrioventricular septal defect is strongly linked with Down syndrome.

q: A newborn whose mother has lupus has a heart rate of 55/min. What is the likely diagnosis?
e: Anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies damage the conduction system.

q: A newborn becomes cyanosed on day 3 as the duct closes. The first drug is:
e: Prostaglandin E1 reopens the duct in duct-dependent lesions.
